newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European shares weaken, dollar rebounds.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European shares weaken, dollar rebounds.

text.p: European shares weakened in early trade on Tuesday as doubts about the prospects of a single European currency continued to rattle traders, although the dollar rallied against the mark.

French shares led the way lower and were down around 1.1 percent by 0900 gmt, extending Monday's steep fall on concerns over the euro and France's wrangling about the stability pact designed to ensure budgetary discipline under economic and monetary union (EMU).
"There are no buyers around, there's no support for the market," said a French broker.
In Paris, the blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 30.11 points at 2,656.09 at 0900 GMT. The index had opened down 0.56 percent.
The London and Frankfurt share markets were also down by 0.4 and 0.1 percent respectively.

Europe's share markets appeared to have decoupled from Wall Street, which hit another record close overnight when the Dow Jones index of leading U.S. stocks ended 42.72 points higher at 7,478.50. it was the second straight record finish for the blue chip index.
The Dow has surged more than 1,000 points since the start of 1997 and is now benefiting from the dollar's recent weakness which is boosting shares in big U.S. exporting companies.

The latest bout of worries over EMU surfaced on Monday when French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn and other European Union officials said a delay in approving the stability pact was not a precursor to renegotiating it.

But traders will remain jittery about the outlook for EMU until France gives its verdict on the stability pact. French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Tuesday that Paris needed more than a week to study the pact and carry out an audit of state finances.

German shares got off to a rocky start in bourse trade, falling slightly in volatile trade due to worries about the single European currency and the future of the ruling Bonn coalition. The 30-share DAX index was down 13.67 points at 3,653.76 by 0900 gmt.
"I do not expect more losses at the moment but some uneven trading as the market decides what to do next," said one Stuttgart-based trader after Monday's steep drop.

In London, the FTSE index of leading British stocks opened slightly firmer on the back of Wall Street's advance but dealers said investors were turning increasingly cautious and the market swung both sides of Monday's close.
In currencies, the dollar rebounded from the low it set against the mark on Monday, although its gains were expected to be limited as long as talk of a delay to EMU persists.
France's plea for time to consider the stability pact on Monday boosted the mark against other European currencies and the dollar.
While short covering lifted the dollar from its lows against the mark, it will struggle to extend its gains until an accord on the stability pact is reached, analysts said.

"The fundamentals are very supportive of the dollar, and the market is short after the move yesterday," said Lee Ferridge, the currency strategist at Commerzbank. "But given all the doubts about EMU, I don't expect the move to go too far or last too long."
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7095 at 0900 GMT from its 1.7020 low on Monday and 1.7063 late yesterday in Europe. Dollar/yen was at 112.55, little changed from Monday.
The dollar was steady against the yen after U.S. officials repeated their support for a strong U.S. currency and a Japanese officials spoke out against excessive currency moves.
Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said currency moves have been excessive and that Japan would combat excessive swings in an appropriate and timely way.
